sentence: That distinction matters for the same reason it matters in the [irregular preterite verbs](/irregular-preterite-verbs-spanish/): the preterite has families that swap in a new stem and share a core ending pattern, with -eron for the third-person plural of j-stem verbs, while the imperfect has almost none of that.
note: Target documents changed preterite stems, shared ending family and j-stem -eron; comparison does not assert all irregular paradigms identical.
target_quote: 'Notice there\'s no accent on estuve or estuvo, unlike a regular -ar preterite like hablé or habló. Estuve and estuvo stress the penultimate syllable and end in a vowel, so the general spelling rule leaves them without a tilde. Hablé and habló stress the final syllable and end in a vowel, which requires a tilde. The endings themselves, for every one of these irregular stems, still closely echo the [regular -er/-ir preterite set](/spanish-preterite-endings/), with -e and -o in place of -í and -ió for yo and él. The j-stem verbs finish their ellos/ellas/ustedes forms in -eron, omitting the i of -ieron.',
